label: early original/<DEL> step right after d, f, r or p (or two steps after d/f)
explanation: Fires during the input phase (89% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (10%). It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.2% of mass) and never at t=0. It is driven by the previous input token: the active rate is 43% after d, 41% after f, 36% after r and 23% after p (s is weaker), against a 7% base rate. Some activation carries over to the step two after d or f. It is strongly limited to early positions: rate peaks at t=2-3 and is near zero from t>=7. The largest activations come at <DEL> in short sequences that end in ...f d or ...x d, i.e. <DEL> directly after d, and at early steps. The input token at the current step barely matters. The predicate (input phase or <DEL>, t<=5, previous token in {d,f,r,p} or the token two back in {d,f}) gets dev F1 0.76, precision 0.77, mass recall 0.87. Misses are mostly weak activations after other tokens; false positives are mostly at later positions, where the same contexts often stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: d, f, r, p, s, a; least: n, z, 2, g) and the input two steps back (most: d, f, r, p, u, s; least: j, z, 2, g); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, t=4.
